title: UniFast-HGR: Scalable and Efficient Maximal Correlation for Multimodal Models
claim: A costly covariance-whitening computation is replaced by a cheaper batch-space surrogate, with a further projected variant for low memory.
layout: 3 columns, top-to-bottom flow, dashed prior path left, color-coded branches
description: A flowchart with three vertical columns of rounded boxes, each color-coded. A shared 'features F,G' box sits at the top center. The left purple column has dashed boxes and dotted arrows for the classical covariance path: K×K covariance, whitening eigen-solve, then HGR-style score. The center blue column is the UniFast-HGR full surrogate: batch center + l2 normalize, batch Gram, remove diagonal (D_off / TSS), then structural cosine UniFast-HGR score. The right green column is the Opt-HGR projected surrogate: random projection, projected off-diagonal estimate, then OptFast-HGR score. Dashed horizontal arrows labeled 'surrogate' and 'approx' link the scores. A bottom row of three summary boxes reads K-space covariance, local-batch Gram-space dependence and low-memory estimate. The eye goes first to the top box, then down the center blue column.
caption: Conceptual computation paths. The dashed left branch follows the classical covariance-based HGR pipeline. UniFast-HGR replaces covariance whitening with centered and ℓ2normalized Gram-space dependence, then suppresses invariant diagonal self-correlation through Doff. OptFast-HGR approximates the same off-diagonal structural signal through random projection to reduce memory and large-batch overhead.
abstract: This paper presents UniFast-HGR, a scalable surrogate for Hirschfeld--Gebelein--R\'enyi (HGR) maximal correlation in high-dimensional multimodal learning. The method replaces explicit covariance whitening with centered and $\ell_2$-normalized cosine alignment, rewrites the covariance interaction in local-batch Gram space, and removes invariant diagonal self-correlation through Trivial Spectrum Suppression (TSS). This reformulation preserves the standardized dependence-maximization target of HGR-style learning while replacing the finite-sample whitening estimator with a differentiable local-batch objective whose dominant structural cost is $O(m^2K)$ for local batch size $m$ and feature dimension $K$. OptFast-HGR further reduces the practical memory burden by estimating the off-diagonal structural term through stochastic projection. Experiments across retrieval, image classification, remote sensing segmentation, and multimodal emotion recognition show consistent gains over covariance-based HGR/CCA variants and contrastive or neural MI-estimator objectives on strong multimodal backbones, while microbenchmarks confirm stable behavior at extreme feature dimensions.
